objective: T-20260929-81: do two IPO aftermarket calendar windows (long around the 25-calendar-day quiet-period expiry; short after a >= +20% first-week pop) still pay net of tiered spread and borrow in 2016-2026, and especially from 2024, using the local T-21 IPO event table? Cheapest event-study negation test first; no ledger unless a family clears the frozen numbers.

sources.applicability: Defines the A-family calendar (QP day, market-adjusted CAR) and the numbers the plan's stop conditions are set against.
sources.claim: Bradley, Jordan and Ritter (J. Finance 2003): 1,611 US IPOs 1996-2000; quiet period ends after the 25th calendar day (day 0 = 26th calendar day or first trading day thereafter); analyst coverage initiated immediately for 76%; initiated firms earn a five-day (-2,+2) abnormal return of 4.1% vs 0.1% for firms with no coverage (Nasdaq-adjusted); abnormal returns concentrate in the days just before expiry. Excludes offers with file-range midpoint below $8.

sources.applicability: Directly weakens the mechanism for the whole local sample; motivates a non-gating diagnostic window at day 10 and a hard stop if the day-25 window shows nothing.
sources.claim: FINRA Regulatory Notice 15-30 (August 2015): Rule 2241 reduces the 40-day and 25-day IPO quiet periods to a minimum of 10 days after the offering for members that acted as underwriter or dealer (effective 2015-12-24). The mandatory research blackout that made day 25 a hard date in 1996-2000 no longer exists in the 2016-2026 sample; any day-25 clustering of initiations would be a convention, not a rule.
